title: PECARN Pediatric Head Injury Rule
sources: Kuppermann N et al. Lancet 2009 (PECARN); validated PECARN 2019 (PREDICT/pooled)
purpose: Identifies children < 18 years with minor blunt head trauma (GCS 14–15) who are at very low risk of clinically important traumatic brain injury (ciTBI) and can safely skip a CT. Apply the AGE-SPECIFIC logic in the interpretation — the point count here is a helper for the number of predictors present. Use within 24 h of injury.

items.label: EITHER AGE — GCS ≤ 14, OR other signs of altered mental status (agitation, somnolence, repetitive questioning, slow response), OR (age < 2) palpable skull fracture / (age ≥ 2) any sign of basilar skull fracture
Age < 2: LOC ≥ 5 seconds  ·  Age ≥ 2: any history of LOC
Age < 2: non-frontal (occipital / parietal / temporal) scalp haematoma  ·  Age ≥ 2: history of vomiting
EITHER AGE — Severe mechanism: MVC with ejection / rollover / fatality, pedestrian or unhelmeted cyclist struck, fall > 0.9 m if < 2 y (> 1.5 m if ≥ 2 y), or head struck by a high-impact object
Age < 2: not acting normally per the parent  ·  Age ≥ 2: severe headache

interpretation.label: No predictors — ciTBI risk ≈ 0.02% (age < 2) / 0.05% (age ≥ 2). CT NOT recommended. Discharge with head-injury advice

Intermediate — one or more of the minor predictors (LOC, non-frontal haematoma or vomiting, severe mechanism, behaviour change or severe headache) but NO GCS ≤ 14 / AMS / skull-fracture sign. ciTBI risk ≈ 0.9%. Either OBSERVE for 4–6 h or CT, using shared decision-making — favour observation for a single isolated finding, an improving child, parental preference, and age ≥ 3 months; favour CT for multiple findings, worsening symptoms, or age < 3 months
High risk — GCS ≤ 14, altered mental status, OR (age < 2) palpable skull fracture / (age ≥ 2) signs of basilar skull fracture. ciTBI risk ≈ 4.3–4.4%. CT head IS recommended

notes: ciTBI = death, neurosurgery, intubation > 24 h for the head injury, or hospital admission ≥ 2 nights with TBI on CT. PECARN does NOT apply to trivial mechanisms (ground-level falls, walking/running into stationary objects with no signs/symptoms other than scalp abrasion), penetrating trauma, known brain tumours, pre-existing neuro disorders, or suspected non-accidental trauma — use clinical judgement / lower the imaging threshold for those. Isolated frontal scalp haematoma in an otherwise well child ≥ 3 months is low-risk. Observation before CT roughly halves CT use without missing ciTBI.
buildNote: Age-specific decision tree — the high-risk item is weighted 5 to force the 'CT recommended' band; minor predictors are 1 each for the intermediate band.
